quests.instruction: Correct the grammatical error in the sentence.
quests.passage: I [making] a video call when the internet suddenly disconnected.
quests.hint: Think about an action that was already in progress when something else interrupted it.
quests.explanation: The past continuous needs both 'was' and the -ing form: 'was making,' not just 'making.'

quests.instruction: Correct the grammatical error in the sentence.
quests.passage: While she [was save] her files, the computer froze completely.
quests.hint: Think about an ongoing action interrupted by another event, and check the verb ending.
quests.explanation: The past continuous requires the -ing form after 'was': 'was saving,' not 'was save.'

quests.instruction: Correct the grammatical error in the sentence.
quests.passage: What [you were] doing online at midnight last night?
quests.hint: In questions, the auxiliary verb usually comes before the subject.
quests.explanation: Past continuous questions invert the auxiliary and subject: 'were you,' not 'you were.'

quests.instruction: Correct the grammatical error in the sentence.
quests.passage: I [waiting] when the doctor finally walked into the room.
quests.hint: Think about an ongoing action that was happening when another event occurred, and check for a missing word.
quests.explanation: The past continuous needs 'was' plus the -ing form: 'was waiting,' not just 'waiting.'

quests.instruction: Correct the grammatical error in the sentence.
quests.passage: She felt dizzy while she [were running] on the treadmill yesterday.
quests.hint: The subject 'she' is singular, so check the matching form of 'be' in the past continuous.
quests.explanation: With the singular subject 'she,' the past continuous uses 'was,' not 'were': 'was running.'

quests.instruction: Correct the grammatical error in the sentence.
quests.passage: They [was checking] the patient's blood pressure when the alarm went off.
quests.hint: The subject 'they' is plural, so check the matching form of 'be' in the past continuous.
quests.explanation: With the plural subject 'they,' the past continuous uses 'were,' not 'was': 'were checking.'

quests.instruction: Correct the grammatical error in the sentence.
quests.passage: We [is going to] watch the new superhero movie this weekend.
quests.hint: The subject 'we' is plural; think about the matching form of 'going to.'
quests.explanation: With the plural subject 'we,' the correct form is 'are going to,' not 'is going to.'

quests.instruction: Correct the grammatical error in the sentence.
quests.passage: My sister [are going to] join a dance class starting next month.
quests.hint: The subject 'my sister' is singular; think about the matching form of 'going to.'
quests.explanation: With the singular subject 'my sister,' the correct form is 'is going to,' not 'are going to.'

quests.instruction: Correct the grammatical error in the sentence.
quests.passage: I [is going to] buy tickets for the concert first thing tomorrow morning.
quests.hint: The subject is 'I'; think about the matching form of 'going to.'
quests.explanation: With the subject 'I,' the form of 'going to' is always 'am going to,' not 'is going to.'

quests.instruction: Correct the grammatical error in the sentence.
quests.passage: She [are going to] call you back as soon as she finishes her meeting.
quests.hint: The subject 'she' is singular; think about the matching form of 'going to.'
quests.explanation: With the singular subject 'she,' the correct form is 'is going to,' not 'are going to.'

quests.instruction: Correct the grammatical error in the sentence.
quests.passage: We [is going to] send you the documents by email later this afternoon.
quests.hint: Match the plural subject 'we' to the correct form of 'going to.'
quests.explanation: 'We' is plural, so 'going to' takes 'are,' not the singular form 'is.'

quests.instruction: Correct the grammatical error in the sentence.
quests.passage: I [are going to] explain everything clearly once we meet in person.
quests.hint: Remember which form of 'going to' always goes with the subject 'I.'
quests.explanation: With the subject 'I,' 'going to' always takes the form 'am going to,' not 'are going to.'

quests.instruction: Correct the grammatical error in the sentence.
quests.passage: Don't worry, I [will to help] you carry those heavy bags upstairs.
quests.hint: 'Will' is followed directly by the base form of the verb, with no extra word in between.
quests.explanation: 'Will' is followed straight by the base verb form: 'will help,' never 'will to help.'

quests.instruction: Correct the grammatical error in the sentence.
quests.passage: I think it [wills rain] later this evening; the sky looks quite dark.
quests.hint: 'Will' never changes form for different subjects, no matter what they are.
quests.explanation: 'Will' stays the same for every subject and never takes an -s ending: 'will rain,' not 'wills rain.'

quests.instruction: Correct the grammatical error in the sentence.
quests.passage: She [will probably to be] home by seven, according to her last message.
quests.hint: 'Will' is followed directly by the base verb, even with an adverb like 'probably' in between.
quests.explanation: 'Will' takes the base verb form even with an adverb inserted: 'will probably be,' not 'will probably to be.'

quests.instruction: Correct the grammatical error in the sentence.
quests.passage: I promise I [will to study] harder for the next exam.
quests.hint: No word should separate 'will' from the base verb that follows it.
quests.explanation: 'Will' is followed directly by the base verb form: 'will study,' never 'will to study.'

quests.instruction: Correct the grammatical error in the sentence.
quests.passage: Our teacher says the test results [wills be] ready by Friday afternoon.
quests.hint: The modal 'will' stays exactly the same regardless of the subject.
quests.explanation: 'Will' stays the same for every subject: 'will be,' not 'wills be.'

quests.instruction: Correct the grammatical error in the sentence.
quests.passage: Don't worry about the presentation - I [will to help] you practice tonight.
quests.hint: 'Will' is followed directly by the base verb, with no 'to' in between.
quests.explanation: 'Will' is never followed by 'to': the correct form is 'will help,' not 'will to help.'

quests.instruction: Correct the grammatical error in the sentence.
quests.passage: This is [the most difficultest] project I have ever worked on at this company.
quests.hint: Longer adjectives form the superlative with 'the most' alone, never combined with an -est ending.
quests.explanation: Long adjectives like 'difficult' use only 'the most': 'the most difficult,' never adding -est as well.

quests.instruction: Correct the grammatical error in the sentence.
quests.passage: She is [most hard-working] employee in our entire department.
quests.hint: Superlatives comparing one thing to a whole group require the article 'the.'
quests.explanation: Superlatives always include 'the': 'the most hard-working,' not just 'most hard-working.'

quests.instruction: Correct the grammatical error in the sentence.
quests.passage: That was [the longuest] meeting of the entire year, in my opinion.
quests.hint: Short adjectives form the superlative with -est alone, added directly to the adjective.
quests.explanation: 'Long' becomes 'longest' in the superlative; the spelling 'longuest' is simply incorrect.

quests.instruction: Correct the grammatical error in the sentence.
quests.passage: This is [most beautiful] beach I have ever visited in my entire life.
quests.hint: Don't forget 'the' when forming a superlative about an entire group.
quests.explanation: Superlatives always include 'the': 'the most beautiful,' not just 'most beautiful.'

quests.instruction: Correct the grammatical error in the sentence.
quests.passage: That mountain is [the most high] peak in the entire country.
quests.hint: Short adjectives form the superlative with -est alone, not with 'the most.'
quests.explanation: Short adjectives like 'high' use the -est ending: 'the highest,' not 'the most high.'

quests.instruction: Correct the grammatical error in the sentence.
quests.passage: Our guide showed us [the most fastest] route through the old city center.
quests.hint: Short adjectives form the superlative with -est alone, never combined with 'the most.'
quests.explanation: Short adjectives like 'fast' use only -est: 'the fastest,' never both 'the most' and '-est' together.

quests.instruction: Correct the grammatical error in the sentence.
quests.passage: Children [mustn't] wear a seatbelt every time they are in the car.
quests.hint: Think about whether this rule requires something or forbids something.
quests.explanation: This is a required safety rule, so it needs 'must,' not 'mustn't,' which expresses prohibition.

quests.instruction: Correct the grammatical error in the sentence.
quests.passage: You [must] leave young children alone near the swimming pool, for their safety.
quests.hint: Think about whether this sentence forbids something dangerous or requires it.
quests.explanation: This describes something dangerous that should be avoided, so it needs 'mustn't,' not 'must.'

quests.instruction: Correct the grammatical error in the sentence.
quests.passage: In our family, everyone [mustn't] help clean up after dinner together.
quests.hint: Think about whether this household rule requires participation or forbids it.
quests.explanation: This is a firm family rule requiring participation, so it needs 'must,' not 'mustn't.'

quests.instruction: Correct the grammatical error in the sentence.
quests.passage: Customers [mustn't] show their receipt in order to return an item.
quests.hint: Think about whether this store policy requires something or forbids it.
quests.explanation: This describes a required condition for returns, so it needs 'must,' not 'mustn't.'

quests.instruction: Correct the grammatical error in the sentence.
quests.passage: You [must] touch the items in the glass display case, according to the sign.
quests.hint: Think about whether this is something store staff would forbid.
quests.explanation: This describes a prohibition against touching items, so it needs 'mustn't,' not 'must.'

quests.instruction: Correct the grammatical error in the sentence.
quests.passage: Shoppers [mustn't] wear a mask if the store requires it by policy.
quests.hint: Think about whether store policy requires this action or forbids it.
quests.explanation: This describes a requirement set by store policy, so it needs 'must,' not 'mustn't.'
